summary: Stub npm package exfiltrates host identifiers to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint at install and require time
details: The package presents itself as a 'Compatibility shim' but ships no real functionality: its main module exports a Proxy returning no-ops for every property access, and the only observable behavior is a beacon. `beacon.cjs` collects host identifiers (hostname, install path, cwd, node version) and POSTs them as JSON to the hardcoded plain-HTTP bare-IP endpoint http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc. The beacon fires on `npm install` via the declared `postinstall` script (`node beacon.cjs`) and again on `require()` of the package via a top-level `require('./beacon.cjs').fire()` call in `index.js`. The package name, description, and comments labeling the behavior as 'build-provenance' do not match the shipped code, which is a name-grab plus install-time and import-time callback to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
